editorial_note: The two source-labeled axiomatizations are equivalent: complements follow from X\A, while ordinary countable unions can be made disjoint by replacing A_n with A_n\(⋃_{k<n}A_k). Finite unions needed in that reduction follow from difference/complement closure. The countable-disjoint-union condition must not be read as unrestricted union of arbitrary pairwise-disjoint indexed sets; the indexing is countable. σ-algebra is a family of subsets of a specified X, not automatically the measurable-space pair (X,Σ). Source section: Definition 1
text: For a set X, a σ-algebra on X is a family Σ⊆P(X) such that X∈Σ, A∈Σ implies X\A∈Σ, and ⋃_{n≥1}A_n∈Σ whenever every A_n∈Σ.

text: Equivalently, a family Σ⊆P(X) is a σ-algebra if X∈Σ, it is closed under differences A\B for A,B∈Σ, and it is closed under countable unions of pairwise disjoint members.

editorial_note: The open-cover and closed-set finite-intersection formulations are equivalent by taking complements and applying De Morgan's laws. Neither requires Hausdorff separation. Some traditions reserve 'compact' for Hausdorff plus quasi-compact; such terminology must be recorded as a context-specific convention rather than silently imported into the general topological definition. Euclidean closed-and-bounded is an equivalence theorem special to R^n, not the defining general-topology requirement. Source section: Definition 1
text: A topological space X is compact if every open cover of X contains a finite subfamily whose union is X.

text: Equivalently, X is compact if every family of closed subsets of X that has the finite intersection property has nonempty total intersection.
